This page says who owns each step from a layout to a report, and how a Palace
run and an AEDT run are prepared, run and read back. Which folder is which
stage is on the [code map](code-map.qmd); what an area must not take over is
on [Ownership by area](ownership.qmd). Exact formats and rules are on the
contract pages this page links.

## Entry packages and one model {#current-package-structure}

SCGSim has four entry packages: `scgsim.geometry`, `scgsim.palace`,
`scgsim.aedt` and `scgsim.visualization`. A name is public when one of them
exports it or a contract page documents it; that a module can be imported
does not make it public. The supported entry, and what a call below it must
guarantee itself, is stated once, in
[Supported scope](../reference/supported-scope.qmd#supported-entry); the
geometry builder `scgsim.geometry.sgb` sits below it.
`python -m scgsim.aedt.run` is a supported command, the entry of the AEDT
transaction.

Palace and AEDT solve models made by the same builder:

1. `scgsim.geometry` turns a layout and a stack into a `GeometryPlan`, whose
   snapshot is the prepared input (`geometry/source`), and interprets it into
   the effective input (`geometry/interpretation`, with the junction
   partition of `geometry/junctions`).
2. `geometry/sgb` builds the 3D model from the effective input
   (`build_sgb_geometry`), with the Surface-EPR bands that
   `geometry/surface_epr` requests. Line and circular-arc boundaries stay exact;
   a spline is refused.
3. Palace meshes the model's XAO with `scgsim.meshing`, which reads it and its
   sidecar through `contracts`, never through SGB or a backend.
4. AEDT builds its model with the same builder, on Route A for
   `modeling="thin_film"` and Route C for `"solid"`, exports it as a STEP with a
   guard file (`aedt/preparation`: `prepare_sgb_model`, then `export_aedt_step`), carries
   it in the handoff, and, inside AEDT, imports it and makes every assignment
   from the sidecar (`aedt/runtime/families/sgb_import.py`). AEDT builds no
   geometry of its own.

## Who owns which fact {#contract-boundaries}

| Fact | Owner |
|---|---|
| Materials, layers, fabrication, thicknesses and the 3D stack | The PDK |
| Entities, their polygon and curve boundaries, ports and selectors | The component |
| Named occurrences and the final `Net → Entity` map | The notebook's `GeometryPlan` |
| The immutable prepared input | The plan's snapshot (`GeometryBuildInput`) |
| Geometry names, topology and the Route A, B and C surfaces | `scgsim.geometry.sgb` |
| The tetrahedral mesh, its sizing and its quality threshold | `scgsim.meshing` |
| Run identity, handoff, execution profile and receipt | The run contract of each backend |
| What a returned number means physically | The solver it came from; never one quantity flattened across solvers |
| Public component-simulation notebooks | OrcaPen SC PDK |

## Semantic facts {#internal-semantic-facts}

`scgsim.semantics` holds facts that do not depend on a solver: the
revision-bound snapshot, the Route A projection, the EPR records and
`SParameters`, the S-parameter record every driven solver returns, with its one
Touchstone writer. Each backend reads its own files into that record. It uses
the standard library only and imports no SGB, Palace, AEDT or native code. A
fact whose revision does not match is refused rather than rebound. A native
tag a backend reports stays an observation; it never decides contact or
identity.

## Notebooks and mesh quality {#notebook-and-implementation-boundaries}

Public notebooks call the entry packages directly; their rules are the
[notebook contract](notebook-contract.qmd). Mesh quality is the
`scgsim.meshing` audit `mesh()` runs: it holds the threshold and writes the
quality report ([Mesh quality](../reference/specs/mesh-quality.qmd)). Whether
a result has converged physically is a separate question, which the
convergence declaration of a run answers.

## Palace preparation lifecycle {#palace-preparation-lifecycle}

`ElectrostaticSim`, `EigenmodeSim` and `DrivenSim` own their mutable mesh,
config, resolved-port and handoff state. All three are subclasses of one private
base, `scgsim.palace.simulation.core.PalaceSimulation`, which holds what they share:
`set_plan`, `set_output_dir`, `set_route`, `set_mesh`, `input_summary()`,
`mesh()`, `simulation_drc`, `mesh_summary()` and `prepare_handoff()`. Each
problem file (`simulation/electrostatic.py`, `simulation/eigenmode.py`,
`simulation/driven.py`) adds
only its setters, its numerical defaults and its `write_config()`. The vacuum
region and the Surface-EPR specs are the plan's
(`GeometryPlan.set_vacuum_region`, `GeometryPlan.set_surface_epr`); the
simulation reads them from the snapshot it is bound to.

The lifecycle is one table, `scgsim.palace.simulation.lifecycle`:

| Stage | Reached by | A setter falls back here when |
|---|---|---|
| `UNBOUND` | creating the simulation | |
| `BOUND` | `set_plan` | `mesh()` reads its value: output folder, route, mesh controls, Eigenmode ports |
| `MESHED` | `mesh()` | only `write_config()` reads its value |
| `CONFIG_WRITTEN` | `write_config()` | |
| `HANDED_OFF` | `prepare_handoff()` | |

A call made before the stage it needs is refused with a message that names
the call to make first. Route B is the default for both problems, and Surface
EPR is computed only when the plan was given specs.

`mesh()` and `write_config()` first fall back, discarding what they will
rebuild, and only then check what they need. `write_config()` writes each
metadata file through a temporary file and `config.json` last
(`config.files.persist_problem_files`), so a run folder whose `config.json`
is new has every metadata file it needs and no stale one. This holds file by
file; it is not one transaction for the whole folder, and falling back in
memory does not delete an older file on disk.

A simulation holds its settings as frozen values, each checked when it is
built and defined in the stage that reads it first:

| Attribute | Type | Stage | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `numerical` | `NumericalControls` | `config.numerical` | `write_config()`, `mesh_summary()` (FEM order) |
| `surface_epr_specs` (from the bound plan) | `SurfaceEprSpecs` | `source.surface_epr` | `mesh()` (the bands), `write_config()` (the `Dielectric` rows) |
| `epr_request` (Eigenmode) | `EprRequest` | `config.index` | `write_config()` (`check_epr_request` and the index map) |

`write_config()` gives the config builder a `ConfigInput` (the mesh, the
materials, the Surface-EPR specs and the numerical controls) and the problem's
`EigenmodeSettings` or `ElectrostaticSettings`. The builder returns one index
record per config section (`PortEntry`, `TerminalEntry`, `EnergyEntry`,
`SurfaceEprEntry`), which `palace_index_map.json` holds.

Every stage takes the run folder's layout from one module,
`scgsim.contracts.palace_run_folder`: the path and schema of each file, the
handoff identity (`HandoffIdentity`) that the handoff writes and
`resolve_palace_result` checks, and one record per problem (`PalaceProblem`:
`EIGENMODE`, `ELECTROSTATIC`). Code that differs by problem reads that record
instead of comparing problem names; its `written_families` decides which
tables a run must return. The module imports only the standard library, so
`palace/run` can copy it into the run folder: the receipt recorder
(`metadata/record_palace_return.py`) and, for a run with a convergence
declaration, the convergence runner (`metadata/run_palace_until_converged.py`)
need only a Python interpreter on the solver host.

After the run, `palace/results` reads the returned folder into checked
records (`ResolvedRunData`), and `palace/reports` builds what a person reads
(`resolve_palace_result` returns `ResolvedPalaceResult`, with its trust,
physics and benchmark views). Every public name is imported from
`scgsim.palace`.

## AEDT execution lifecycle {#aedt-execution-lifecycle}

`python -m scgsim.aedt.run` calls `scgsim.aedt.runtime.transaction.main`.
One transaction runs one prepared handoff, in this order:

1. validate the handoff before the receipt changes;
2. start the receipt, record the runtime source, import PyAEDT and open the
   Desktop it owns;
3. dispatch one solver family (HFSS, Q3D or Q2D), which imports the SGB model
   where the request has one, solves and exports;
4. record the result, release the Desktop and finish the receipt. A failure
   of the family is kept as the run's failure even when the release fails too.

The families do not import the transaction and do not start a Desktop; the
shared native calls below them are in `aedt/runtime/native`. HFSS Eigenmode
and EPR share one setup-control mapping; the
[setup-control contract](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#aedt-family-setup-controls)
lists the controls of each family. A Q3D run can be asked to stop or abort and
save its project (`request_q3d_stop_and_save`, `request_q3d_abort_and_save`);
the rules are in the
[AEDT runtime](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#q3d-user-requested-stopabort-and-save).

### Request-scoped AEDT version selection

A request names its AEDT version, `"2023.2"` or `"2024.2"`, with no default
and no fallback to the other; the version belongs to that request and its
transaction, not to the process. `versions.py` holds the pinned transport
profile of each; the
[version contract](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#aedt-version-selection)
gives the transport settings.

### Prepared-native HFSS EPR batch workflow

An HFSS EPR model can be prepared on a workstation and solved on another host:

prepare and release the native model (transaction) → package one model
(`aedt/batch.py`, `prepare_native_batch`) → solve it with the standalone
runner, without a PyAEDT Desktop (`run_native_batch`) → collect the returned
project on an owned copy, in a new transaction (`collect_native_batch`) →
resolve and present offline.

Each package, attempt and result belongs to one model; a sweep is several
packages. `aedt/runtime/batch_protocol.py` is the standard-library file
protocol, and `aedt/runtime/batch_runner.py` is copied into the package and
runs the solver without importing PyAEDT or SCGSim. The
[batch contract](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#prepared-native-hfss-epr-batch)
defines the package, the attempt and the collection.

### Receipts and runtime source {#receipts-and-runtime-source}

A handoff declares receipt schema `scgsim.aedt.receipt.v3`, and preparation
and execution each record the runtime source they ran
(`aedt/results/provenance.py`, `aedt/results/runtime_inventory.py`). What a
receipt and a runtime source hold, and which older formats are refused, is in
[Provenance](provenance.qmd) and
[Current formats](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#current-formats); how an
EPR run binds the native mode and its pass cache is in
[Mode binding and pass cache](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#mode-binding-and-pass-cache).

See [Ownership by area](ownership.qmd) for what each area must not take over,
and [Preview the geometry](../guides/preview-the-geometry.qmd) for the static
and connected geometry previews.
